source_evidence: Inflation reduces purchasing power, which is a risk for investors receiving a fixed rate of interest. It also can lead to higher interest rates and, in turn, lower market value for existing bonds.
answer: Inflation risk is the chance that rising prices will reduce what you can buy with the interest from a municipal bond that pays a fixed rate. Inflation can also contribute to higher interest rates, which may lower the market value of existing bonds. These are two distinct effects: reduced purchasing power of the bond’s interest and a possible decline in its market value.
